A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the solutions provided by our method are the ones of vanishing viscosity approximation in the absence of a decreasing branch in stress-strain response, while in the presence of such a branch they are the ones obtained by the relaxed variational formulation of Maso-Murat.

, while the solutions provided by the relaxed problem are in general not unique, they can be selected in a coherent way among all possible ones by prescribing the stress-strain law in a decreasing branch.

, for the class of models we are dealing with, the solutions obtained by our method coincide with the ones given by the vanishing viscosity approximation only if the latter are increasing in the stress-strained response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the notion of global stability alone is not enough to guarantee the existence of a solution to the relaxed problem.

the relaxation of the quasivariational inequality characterizing global stability allows to obtain solutions that are globally stable on the whole time interval, without the need of introducing a viscosity term.
global stability, in the form of a suitable stability condition, is a key ingredient in the construction of a well-posed relaxed formulation.
